City Boy Movement Ogun State Chapter Inaugurated Ahead of 2027 Presidential Election

Tosin Odufuwa at CBM Ogun State Inauguration became a notable part of the City Boy Movement’s activities in Ogun State. The event brought together national leaders, state officials, political stakeholders and members of the organisation in Abeokuta.

October 29, 2026 · CBM OGUN

Tosin Odufuwa at CBM Ogun State Inauguration became a notable part of the City Boy Movement’s activities in Ogun State. The event brought together national leaders, state officials, political stakeholders and members of the organisation in Abeokuta.

Odufuwa, the movement’s National Secretary, attended alongside the Director General, Francis Oluwatosin Shoga, and other members of the national leadership. Their participation formed part of the inauguration of the Ogun State Executive Committee.

The event also attracted Ogun State Deputy Governor, Mrs. Noimot Salako-Oyedele, who represented Governor Dapo Abiodun. Senator Solomon Adeola, popularly known as Yayi, who represents Ogun West and is the All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate for Ogun State, also attended.

According to the movement’s announcement, the gathering focused on leadership, grassroots engagement, empowerment and community development. It also reflected the organisation’s efforts to strengthen its state structure and coordinate its activities across Ogun State.

The inauguration offers an opportunity to examine Odufuwa’s role, the leadership structure established in Ogun and the broader significance of grassroots political organisations in Nigeria.

Tosin Odufuwa at CBM Ogun State Inauguration: What Happened?

Tosin Odufuwa attended the inauguration of the City Boy Movement’s Ogun State Executive Committee as the organisation’s National Secretary. The event brought together national and state representatives, including the Ogun State Deputy Governor and Senator Solomon Adeola, to mark the formal inauguration of the state leadership.

The gathering took place in Abeokuta, Ogun State, in early October 2026. Reports on the event identified Ake Palace as the venue for the inauguration activities.

The programme formed part of the movement’s efforts to establish and strengthen its organisational structure in Ogun State. It also provided an opportunity for members and stakeholders to meet the newly inaugurated executives.

The movement described the gathering as a show of unity and participation. It also highlighted grassroots engagement, empowerment and community development as priorities for its activities.

The event was not limited to the formal inauguration. Related activities included the commissioning of the movement’s Ogun State secretariat and an empowerment programme, according to published reports.

These activities placed organisational development and community engagement at the centre of the gathering.

Who Is Tosin Odufuwa?

Tosin Odufuwa is the National Secretary of theCity Boy Movement. He attended the Ogun State executive inauguration as part of the organisation’s national leadership, joining Director General Francis Oluwatosin Shoga and other stakeholders.

His participation placed him among the national representatives present as the movement formally inaugurated its state executive structure.

A national secretary generally supports an organisation’s administrative coordination, documentation and communication between its leadership structures. However, the specific duties assigned to Odufuwa within the movement should be confirmed through its official organisational documents.

At the Ogun event, his presence reflected the involvement of the national leadership in the establishment of the Ogun State executive committee.

National and state structures can play different but complementary roles within an organisation. While national leaders provide coordination at the broader organisational level, state executives focus on activities within their jurisdiction.

The inauguration therefore brought the national and state leadership structures together in one setting.

Why was Odufuwa’s attendance significant?

Odufuwa’s attendance was significant in the context of the movement’s organisational activities. As National Secretary, he represented the national leadership at an event intended to formalise the Ogun State executive structure.

His participation also demonstrated the involvement of national representatives in the movement’s state level activities.

However, attendance alone does not establish the precise responsibilities he performed during the inauguration. Those details would require confirmation from an official programme, statement or interview.

What Is the City Boy Movement?

The City Boy Movement, commonly referred to as CBM, is a political support organisation associated with President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and the Renewed Hope agenda. Its public communications describe a focus on political engagement, grassroots mobilisation and outreach to young people and other community groups.

The organisation has been expanding its activities across Nigerian states through state chapters, leadership structures and public events.

Its Ogun State activities form part of this broader organisational development. The inauguration brought together national leaders and local stakeholders to formalise the state executive structure.

According to the movement’s public communications, its activities include engaging communities and encouraging participation in political processes. Its messaging also refers to empowerment and community development.

These are stated organisational priorities. Their practical impact depends on the programmes delivered, the people reached and the outcomes achieved.

What does CBM’s Ogun State chapter do?

A state chapter gives an organisation a structure for coordinating its activities within a particular state. It can connect national leadership with local members, community stakeholders and other participants.

In Ogun State, the inauguration marked a formal step in establishing the chapter’s executive leadership.

The movement has said it intends to strengthen grassroots engagement and expand its presence across the state. Its stated areas of interest include empowerment and community development.

To assess progress, observers would need information about specific programmes, participation levels, resources and measurable outcomes. An inauguration establishes a leadership structure, but it does not by itself demonstrate the results of future activities.
